text: Figure 5.19: BaseType However, there are other corners of the AUTOSAR meta-model beyond the definition of data types and similar “low-level” information is required elsewhere as well, such that SwBaseType is consequently also used for the modeling of these aspects, for example: • Definition of axes for maps and curves • Definition of record layout • Definition of signal properties on communication buses (see [9, AUTOSAR TPS System T emplate]) • Definition of properties of diagnostic telegrams (see [21, AUTOSAR TPS Diag- nostic Extract T emplate]) • Definition of log and trace messages (see [22, AUTOSAR TPS Log and T race]) • Definition of properties relevant for measurement and calibration (see [6, AUTOSAR TPS BSW ModuleDescriptionT emplate]) • Definition of security events (see [23, AUTOSAR TPS SecurityExtractT emplate]) The diversity of the areas of applicability (as hinted by the list in the previous paragraph) of SwBaseType is also reflected in the set of attributes that are relevant for each of the different areas of applicability , as indicated by [TPS_SWCT_01875]. Please note that in the context of using SwBaseType to define an Implementation- DataType, the attributes • byteOrder • memAlignment are used only if the ImplementationDataType represents a Platform Type . 10As in: close to the bare metal emplate
